page: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal server belonging to the storage-optimized family. It is equipped with 96 physical cores across an arm64 architecture utilizing AWS Neoverse-V2 processors clocked at 2.8 GHz. The architecture provisions one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring dedicated processing for all 96 vCPUs. Memory resources include 768.0 GB of DDR5 RAM, yielding 8.0 GB of system memory per physical core. For localized persistence, the bare-metal host integrates 22,500 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD storage. The network interface supports a baseline throughput of 56 Gbps. Graphical processing units are not present on this hardware configuration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier multithreaded compute and memory subsystem performance. Stress-ng multi-core testing logged 163,934.24, and Geekbench multi-core scored 26,626.0, reflecting strong parallel execution and efficient software compilation under Clang. Uncached memory read bandwidth attained 481.52 GB/sec alongside write bandwidth of 218.23 GB/sec, while cached 16 KB read throughput exceeded 11,000 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates exceptional throughput in data-centric operations, yielding 197.01 million Redis SET operations per second and high static web serving transfer rates. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including single-core Geekbench and compression tasks, remain in average industry percentiles, indicating that raw execution speed depends heavily on concurrent thread utilization.

The server offers favorable cost efficiency for storage-heavy architectures by packaging dense NVMe disk space directly within the physical host, eliminating latency and network transfer overhead associated with attached network volumes. Resource balance strongly favors I/O-intensive and memory-hungry applications, although the lack of hardware acceleration limits suitability for compute jobs reliant on GPUs. The system is well aligned with production workloads requiring high disk write endurance and fast random access, such as distributed NoSQL databases, transactional relational database management systems, real-time analytics engines, in-memory key-value stores, and extensive search indexing clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated physical arm64 AWS Neoverse-V2 cores running at 2.8 GHz. Designed without hyperthreading, each core operates on dedicated hardware paired with an 8 GB per core allocation, totaling 768 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory. The server bundles 22,500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 56 Gbps. In benchmark testing, the instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, static web serving, and database transactions, including Redis SET operations reaching 197 million operations per second. However, single-core processing scores place within average performance tiers. The dense ratio of compute cores, DDR5 memory, and direct NVMe capacity makes the server cost-efficient for heavy I/O operations without relying on external network storage. It is engineered for demanding workloads such as large-scale distributed databases, extensive in-memory caching layers, data warehousing, and high-volume real-time transactional processing.
